changes: absorbed all 462 rulebook concepts: 454 projected, 8 merged with configured assembly, 13 configurator-only parts
declaration order follows the rulebook, so ties decided by order agree

the eight output lines no longer name a service implementer. The five derivation services were REMOVED - deprec_impairment (~208 enumerated entries), contingent_liabilities (~172, its NUMBER only; its narrative disclosure survives), secur_fincl_assets (~91), related_party_receivables (~73), sales_revenues (~18): ~562 hand-enumerated note titles, row captions and formula variants in all. `implemented_by` is therefore deleted from all eight and every figure must now come from configuration. The six cascade-less lines - is_pl__sales_revenues, bs_ca__secur_and_other_fincl_assets_cp, bs_nca__secur_and_other_fincl_assets_ltp, bs_nca__due_from_related_parties_ltp, bs_ca__other_receivables_cp, notes__contingent_liabilities - are now `extracted`, since a `derived` line with neither a cascade nor an implementer is refused by LineItemDef; the two depreciation lines stay `derived` on their own cascades (P1-P5 and COS_P1/COS_P2). Cells these services used to fill go blank until the configuration reads them off a caption - that is the intended outcome, so do not reinstate a service name here. Mirrored in output_csv_hk_line_items_configured.json, which is the assembly half of this file

authored expected_components prose on the 11 exclusive_residual buckets (3-4 caption phrases each, 37 in total): the payload block services.mapping._residual_expectations publishes as "captions_with_no_dedicated_concept" was empty on every statement, so an empty canonical_key was never a licensed answer. Each phrase was checked against all 462 concepts' labels and aliases in its own section; hkfrs_hk_china_ontology.json's wording was NOT copied - "Bank overdrafts", "Pension surplus", "Right-of-use assets", "Biological assets", "Contract liabilities", "Bills receivable", "Merger reserve", "Deposits paid for acquisition of land", "Donations" and "Sales taxes and surcharges" all have dedicated concepts here and would have routed real money into a sweep

replaced the zh aliases on the seven is_retained movement lines. All seven carried the identical list 保留溢利 / 未分配利润 / 留存收益 / 累计亏损 — four spellings of the retained-earnings BALANCE, which is bs_equity__retained_profits' own label and the is_retained SECTION's name, not any movement inside it. Provenance: scripts/enrich_output_csv_primary_aliases.py copies Chinese across by matching the ENGLISH alias, and hkfrs_hk_china_ontology.json's bs_equity__retained_earnings carries exactly those four against 'Retained profits' — which all seven lines then carried. spec_alias_curation._SECTION_NAME_IS_NOT_A_MOVEMENT later denied the English caption; the Chinese it had already pulled across was left stranded. Measured before this: 未分配利润 on a profit_and_loss page matched is_retained__cash_div_pref_shares EXACT at 1.0 (first of seven tied at priority 10) while the captions those lines are actually printed under — 对所有者（或股东）的分配, 提取法定盈余公积 — matched nothing. Each line now carries the CAS 所有者权益变动表 wording for its own movement plus the HK equivalent; the four balance spellings stay on bs_equity__retained_profits alone, which is the refuse-and-redirect the English side already used. The residual bucket is_retained__other_adj_to_retained_profits gets none: residual_framework.prohibitions says it is never populated by an alias match.

moved the English alias 'Undistributed profits' off the six is_retained movement lines and onto bs_equity__retained_profits — the same borrowed-balance defect the zh change above fixed. Measured before this, it was matchable ONLY where it is wrong: 'Undistributed profits' on a profit_and_loss page matched is_retained__cash_div_pref_shares EXACT (first of six tied at priority 10) while on a balance_sheet page it matched NOTHING, because the balance line did not own its own caption. So this denial adds as well as removes: the concept whose Chinese already includes 未分配利润, the exact translation, now answers to the English too and the two scripts agree. AND THE RULEBOOK CARRIED ALL OF IT: output_csv_hk_ontology.json declared 'Undistributed profits' plus the four Chinese spellings on the same seven concepts (40 aliases), and services.ontology_projection.SAME copies aliases/aliases_i18n verbatim — so the zh change above would have been undone by the next scripts/build_line_items.py run. The rulebook is cleaned to match, the projection now curates what it copies, and the ontology conformance test covers all three denial tables instead of two.

opened the statement gate on the seven is_retained movement lines: each now declares statements: [equity_changes, profit_and_loss] where it declared only the section's profit_and_loss. Every one of them is a movement in retained earnings — dividends declared, transfers to statutory reserves, prior-period restatements — which a filing prints in the statement of changes in equity (所有者权益变动表) and not on the income statement, so the gate refused them on the one statement whose captions they are and admitted them on one whose captions they are not. Measured after the change: 提取法定盈余公积 and 对所有者（或股东）的分配 resolve on changes_in_equity AND on profit_and_loss, and still refuse balance_sheet. profit_and_loss is kept rather than replaced because the CSRC's older profit-distribution format prints 利润分配 at the foot of the income statement, and mapping._in_statement admits a concept under ANY statement it declares — so this is a widening, never a move. TWO THINGS TRAVEL WITH IT, both recorded in the commit: services.face_context now folds the equity statement's two spellings (StatementType says equity_changes, the page classifier says changes_in_equity) so the block and the citations for these lines are not silently empty; and stages.map_ontology refuses to claim a row whose every figure is a MATRIX COLUMN, because no consumer publishes such a value — see that refusal for what is still missing.
breaking_changes: the set is now 475 definitions, not 21
metadata.vocabulary_note: INERT ON THE DEFAULT ENGINE. The six scoping blocks in `vocabulary` (section_banners 18, umbrella_banners 1, scope_tokens 12, statement_prefixes 4, statement_spellings 1, exclusive_vocabularies 1 = 37 declarations) are consulted only by services/line_item_matching.Vocabulary, reached only under extraction.mapping_engine = "line_items"; config.py ships "ontology" and config.toml names the setting nowhere, so on the shipped default the answers come from services/mapping's module constants, which 49 call sites across 12 modules read with no set in hand. 16 of the 37 (scope_tokens, statement_prefixes) are a test-pinned mirror of those constants (tests/test_buckets_vocabulary.py). Two exceptions: section_banners is walked on every load by MappingVocabulary.refuse_shadowed_banners, a self-consistency refusal rather than a section-scoping read, and caption_characters (not one of the six) is installed into services/mapping at startup by services/line_item_config, so it is live on both engines.

headings: notes to the consolidated financial statements

umbrella_banners.note: IFRS statements print EQUITY AND LIABILITIES above the Equity, Non-current and Current sub-banners; reading it as equity would refuse every liability line item beneath it.

exclusive_vocabularies.note: IAS 7 divides cash flows into exactly three activities and a statement labels each subtotal with its own, so naming one rules out the others.

normalisation.note: Applied to every candidate row label and every alias before comparison. Folding is what allows a single Chinese alias to cover both scripts.
pipeline: Traditional to Simplified fold (OpenCC t2s) applied to BOTH sides of the comparison, so 銷售成本 and 销售成本 collapse to one key.
Full-width to half-width punctuation; map ╱ ／ ⁄ to /; map （） to (); map 、 to , .
Strip footnote and note markers: trailing digits in parentheses, superscripts, '(note 12)', '附註12', '(附注12)'.
Strip trailing colons and dashes used to introduce sub-captions ('Share of profits and losses of:').
Strip inline unit and currency annotations: "RMB'000", '人民幣千元', '(unaudited)', '（未經審核）'.
Collapse internal whitespace to a single space; strip zero-width characters and soft hyphens.
Join a wrapped caption to its continuation line before matching, then also retain the bare fragment as a fallback candidate.
normalisation.wrapped_caption_rule: On a bilingual HKEX statement a caption printed across two physical lines ('TOTAL COMPREHENSIVE' / '年內全面虧損總額' / 'LOSS FOR THE YEAR') must be reassembled from the value row upward before matching. Match the reassembled string first; only if that fails may the bare fragment be used, and then only against concepts whose include criteria explicitly admit the fragment.

binding.note: Precedence is section-first. A concept can only claim a row printed inside one of its section_scope values.
order: 1. Resolve the statement (balance_sheet / profit_and_loss / cash_flow) from the page or table caption.

2. Resolve the printed section from the nearest preceding section header. If no header is resolvable, the row is unbound: route to review, never guess a section. (A row WITH a resolved section that no concept claims is not unbound — it is swept into that section's residual; see unbound_row_policy.)
3. Restrict the candidate concept set to concepts whose section_scope contains the resolved section.
4. Rule tier: exact normalised alias, then regex_hints, in descending match_priority. Any exclude_hints hit is a hard veto, not a score penalty.
5. Semantic tier over the restricted set only, using definition + include + exclude. Never over the full ontology.
6. Tie between concepts listed in each other's confusable_with: resolve with section_disambiguation; if still tied, emit both as candidates and route to review. Never pick by declaration order.
7. Residual sweep (see residual_framework) runs last, over rows no dedicated concept claimed.
8. Reconcile the section against its reported subtotal.
binding.unbound_row_policy: Route an unclaimed face value only to the residual for its resolved printed section. Never borrow a neighbouring concept or cross a section. After all mapping and gap-closing opportunities, the engine-level face_mapping_contract gives any remaining face value a unique engine_unclassified_face key outside the ontology/template namespaces. This keeps the row stored and reviewable without feeding it into an unrelated calculation. Verified non-additive aggregates replaced by mapped components remain evidence-only.
binding.match_priority: Integer 0-99, higher evaluated first. Long specific captions rank above short generic ones so 'Total assets less current liabilities' cannot be pre-empted by 'Total current liabilities' on token overlap. Residuals are 0 and unreachable by matching.

prompt: Map each line item basis their definition, additional information provided and exclusion criteria. Rely on financial meaning and not just words - these are HKEX / PRC filings.

sign_convention.stored_value: The reported value after paren-to-negative conversion.
sign_convention.expenses_and_outflows: Stored NEGATIVE. This is required by the template: pl_gross_profit = sum(revenue, cost_of_goods_sold) and pl_profit_before_exceptional_items_and_tax = sum(total_income, total_operating_cost, total_non_operating_expense) only hold if expense concepts carry a negative sign.
sign_convention.unsigned_source: Where a filing prints expenses as unsigned positives in a by-nature list, negate on load and set sign_normalised: true on the fact so the transformation is auditable.
sign_convention.either: Subtotals, working-capital movements, fair-value changes, share of results, OCI and net cash flows are sign-indeterminate. Retain the reported sign; never coerce.
sign_convention.validation: A concept whose sign_convention is positive_expected or negative_expected but whose loaded value carries the opposite sign is a review trigger, not an auto-correction.

global_rules.face_only_default: Concepts default to face_only: true. Notes are evidence for a face amount, never an independent source of one, unless note_use is decomposition_allowed.
global_rules.duplicate_fact_rule: The same economic fact on the face and in a note is one fact with multiple evidence references, not two additive values. This also applies to two face captions that report the same amount (see equivalence blocks).
parent_child_allocation: Never load a gross parent and its separately mapped children additively.
Residual = reported parent minus confirmed included children.
Subtract only on explicit inclusion wording, hierarchy, reconciliation or arithmetic support.
If containment is uncertain, retain the parent as evidence and route to review.
global_rules.no_fabricated_split: Never invent a decomposition. Where only a combined figure is reported, load the combined concept and leave the children empty. The one exception is a concept declaring sole_component_of: assigning a whole undifferentiated figure to a single child divides nothing, and it is refused as soon as any sibling child is evidenced on the face or in the subtotal's own note.
global_rules.totals_policy: Compute totals from mutually exclusive concept outputs. Use reported totals only for validation, never as an input to the components.

scope_selection.note: Absent from v1 and a common cause of silent mis-loads on HKEX filings.

entity_scope.rule: Where a statement prints Group and Company columns side by side, take the Group (consolidated) column. Record entity_scope on every fact. Never mix columns within one statement.
company_only_markers: Presence of bs_non_current_assets__investments_in_subsidiaries on the face is strong evidence the column is company-only, since consolidation eliminates it.

period_selection.rule: Identify the current period from the column heading date, not from column position; HKEX filings are not consistently current-first. Load comparatives only into the comparative period slot.
period_selection.restatement_rule: Where a comparative column is labelled restated / 重列 / 經重列, load it as the comparative and set restated: true. Do not overwrite a previously loaded original comparative; keep both with a restatement flag.

units_and_currency.rule: Resolve currency and scale from the statement header, not the cover page, and re-resolve per statement. Persist unit on every fact; never normalise scale silently.
units_and_currency.conflict: If header scale and a printed subtotal are inconsistent by a factor of 1,000, trust neither: route the statement to review.

scope_selection.column_guard: Every fact carries the resolved (entity_scope, period, currency, unit). Two facts for the same canonical_key that differ on any of these are distinct facts, not duplicates.

residual_framework.note: One definition governing the 11 output-template subsection residuals. Each uses an existing template line; no template row is added.

sweep.runs: after all dedicated concepts in the section have been resolved, before section reconciliation
sweep.candidate_set: every printed value row on the FACE of the statement whose resolved section equals the residual's single section_scope value
eligibility: The row printed a value for the selected entity_scope, period, currency and unit.
No dedicated concept whose section_scope contains this section claimed the row.

The row is not a section subtotal, statement total, section header, attribution caption, per-share figure, narrative row, note-reference-only row, truncated caption, an of which breakdown of the row above it (其中：/ of which) or a sub-enumerated component of it (（一）… / 1.… beneath 五、净利润) — each of those amounts is already inside the row above, so sweeping it counts the same money twice.
The row was printed INSIDE this section. A row printed in any other section is ineligible however similar its wording — there is no cross-section rescue.

The row's sign agrees with the section's sign_convention, where the section states one. A row signed against its section is evidence the SECTION is wrong, not the amount, so it goes to review rather than into the bucket — a cost swept into income moves the income subtotal and every total below it.
sweep.plug_behaviour: forbidden — the residual is never computed as (reported subtotal − mapped children)
sweep.literal_others_caption: A row captioned 'Others' / '其他' is simply one unmapped face row and sweeps in as a single component. It gets no privileged treatment and no dedicated concept.

itemisation.rule: The residual's value is the arithmetic sum of its components. Original labels and signs are always retained; a swept row is never relabelled to 'Others'.

reconciliation.identity: reported_section_subtotal − Σ(dedicated concepts in section) − Σ(residual components) = 0
reconciliation.tolerance: one rounding unit per contributing row
reconciliation.on_failure: Emit an unallocated_gap fact carrying the difference and route the section to review. Never adjust the residual, and never adjust a dedicated concept, to close the gap.
reconciliation.sections_without_reported_subtotal: If the section prints no subtotal, the residual is still itemised but is flagged unreconciled and carries lower confidence.

review_triggers: any single component exceeds 2% of |reported section subtotal|
a component label scored at or above the semantic threshold against a dedicated concept but was vetoed by exclude_hints
residual sign is opposite to the section's sign_convention
the section reconciliation emitted an unallocated_gap
prohibitions: Never populated by alias, regex or embedding match.
Never carries a value with no itemised components.
Never absorbs a row a dedicated concept could have claimed but was not tested for — all dedicated concepts in the section must be evaluated first.
Never spans sections, statements, periods, entity scopes or units.

items.label: Due from Related Parties(LTP)
items.definition: Amounts receivable from related parties — balances owed by fellow subsidiaries, the immediate and ultimate holding company, shareholders, directors, associates, joint ventures and other related parties, INCLUDING trade receivables from related parties, and NET of any loss allowance carried against them (淨金額). EXCLUDES ENTRUSTED LOANS (委托贷款) routed through a bank, which the specification excludes in its own words and which have their own columns. Excludes amounts PAYABLE to related parties, transaction volumes for the period (交易金额 / 本期发生额) as opposed to balances, guarantees, and the 关联方组合 row of an expected-credit-loss staging table, whose 账面余额 is a portfolio exposure rather than a balance owed. THE LARGEST VALID OF THREE READINGS of the one quantity: Find 1, the related-party rows the balance sheet itself prints; Find 2, the related-party amounts inside the receivable notes; Find 3, the related-party note's own tabulation, net of its loss allowance. Report the highest of whichever of the three the filing supports, and report NOTHING rather than zero if it supports none — an absent disclosure and a nil balance are not the same fact.
items.decomposition_rule: Decompose only from explicit face or note evidence; never fabricate a split.

cascade.note: MAX_VALID(Find 1, Find 2, Find 3) — the spec's own selection rule, now expressible. The three Finds are three readings of ONE quantity and the fullest disclosure wins, which is why this is a maximum and not a sum: summing them would count the same related-party receivable up to three times. Every term is `any_of`, so a filing that discloses only one of the three still answers with that one, and a filing that discloses none leaves the line empty rather than publishing zero (spec 3.6). `outranks_printed` because no balance sheet prints this quantity: it is related-party amounts extracted from within four receivable captions, net of entrusted loans, and a caption binding this line found something else. cascade.note: The same arithmetic on the OTHER source. Find_1_LTP read from the rows the in-scope notes themselves classify as non-current. Spec 6.1 admits only amounts classified under Non-current Assets, so where a note analyses its own total into current and non-current that analysis is the answer and leads. Less Find_2_LTP. LESS THE CURRENT LINE'S OVERSHOOT. `sub__fa_cp_intermediate_residual` is the amount by which the CURRENT securities arithmetic went below zero, and it belongs here — this is the carry-forward this cascade's notes have always described and no rung ever carried, because until now no line held the quantity. `required`: a filing where the current arithmetic did NOT overshoot has no residual, so this rung dies and the one below answers with no carry-forward — the MISSING_CP_CARRYFORWARD_TO_LTP case. `refuse_negative` because LTP is a carrying amount: a negative one is not a figure a filing asserts, and `refused_rungs` records the refusal so a reviewer can see the rung was declined rather than absent.

cascade.note: Σ(the in-scope note totals) − the non-current portion − the derivatives and other receivables disclosed inside those notes − the fair value hierarchy Level 3 total. Each note total is `any_of`, so a filing printing only some of the in-scope notes still sums the ones it prints; every deduction is an `adjustment`, so one the filing does not disclose does not apply. PASSED OVER WHEN IT COMPUTES BELOW ZERO — a negative securities balance is not a figure a filing asserts, and `refused_rungs` records that this rung was declined rather than absent. Replaces the CP_P1 / CP_P2_MISSING_LEVEL_3 pair: with Level 3 an `adjustment` it subtracts nothing when the hierarchy note is absent, which is all the second rung ever did.
Zero, reached only when the rung above was declined for computing below zero. A constant, so it always resolves — which is what makes it a floor rather than another way to publish nothing.

cascade.note: The spec's primary formula: CP_Gross - CP_Related_Party_Deduction, with every gross component taken on the explicit net-carrying-amount basis (spec 3.2 preference 1). The five gross components are any_of because 5.2 says only add a component when the filing separately identifies it, so whatever subset was disclosed is still the sum. The five related-party legs are adjustments with sign -1: each is read from the SAME note that supplied its own gross component, which is what proves the amount is inside CP_Gross, and none of them can make this rung resolve on its own - a rung holding only a deduction has nothing to deduct it from. Deliberately five paired legs rather than one LTP total, because sections 2 and 5.3 forbid deducting the final Due from Related Parties(LTP) value: that total may include 长期应收款 and non-current loans and advances that lie outside this pool. refuse_negative is set because 5.4 says a negative candidate is a NEGATIVE_RESIDUAL, returned as null and never floored at zero. INTEREST AND DIVIDENDS RECEIVABLE joined as a sixth any_of component, because the line's own definition names them and no term read them: on 000709 the note prints 应收利息, 应收股利 and 其他应收款 as three siblings adding to one 合计, and the line published the net of the third alone — 683,092,791.26 against a balance-sheet 其他应收款 of 913,899,591.26, short by the 230,806,800.00 of 应收股利. `any_of` because 5.2 says only add a component a filing separately identifies, and a note that folds them into its other-receivables row identifies none.

The same formula, reached the second way the spec allows when the other-receivables note prints no explicit net carrying amount: spec 3.2 preference 2, closing balance less loss allowance or bad-debt provision. The gross closing balance is required, and the loss allowance is an adjustment with sign -1 - it is a negative row that belongs in the arithmetic, not in the veto list, and a filing that states its balance is already net or that no allowance applies still resolves this rung as gross less nothing. The other four components stay on their net-carrying-amount children and stay any_of, and the five related-party legs deduct exactly as in CP_P1. Second in order because the spec ranks the explicit net amount above the derived one; the first rung that resolves wins, so this fires only when CP_P1 found no explicit net figure. refuse_negative for the same NEGATIVE_RESIDUAL reason. INTEREST AND DIVIDENDS RECEIVABLE joined as a sixth any_of component, because the line's own definition names them and no term read them: on 000709 the note prints 应收利息, 应收股利 and 其他应收款 as three siblings adding to one 合计, and the line published the net of the third alone — 683,092,791.26 against a balance-sheet 其他应收款 of 913,899,591.26, short by the 230,806,800.00 of 应收股利. `any_of` because 5.2 says only add a component a filing separately identifies, and a note that folds them into its other-receivables row identifies none.

cascade.note:
READ FROM THE RELATED-PARTY NOTE, which is the only place a mainland filing states it. This line carried nothing but its own template label and four COMPOUND aliases enumerating every kind of related party at once ("Due to related parties / Associates / Jointly controlled entities / fellow subsidiaries/Affiliates"), and no filing prints that — so it was empty on every filing in the corpus.

A DERIVED PARENT IS UNMATCHABLE BY CAPTION, and that is the shipped design rather than a side effect: `mapping._computed_parent` forbids it so that a figure cannot arrive by a route that skips every rung and loses which disclosure it came from, and it says where a caption belongs instead — on the PART. The consequence is measurable here: China SCE prints "Due to related parties 應付關聯方款項" 2,588,416 on the face of its balance sheet, and that row now reaches no concept. It used to be swept into `bs_cl__other_current_liabilities` — a related-party payable published as an unexplained remainder — and it is now refused from there by the residual's own "dedicated not tested" prohibition and reported for review naming this line. Recovering it properly needs a FACE part, the shape `sub__rp_find_1` declares for the receivable and which nothing fills yet.

cascade.note:
READ FROM THE RELATED-PARTY NOTE, which is the only place a mainland filing states it. This line carried nothing but its own template label and four COMPOUND aliases enumerating every kind of related party at once ("Due to related parties / Associates / Jointly controlled entities / fellow subsidiaries/Affiliates"), and no filing prints that — so it was empty on every filing in the corpus.

A DERIVED PARENT IS UNMATCHABLE BY CAPTION, and that is the shipped design rather than a side effect: `mapping._computed_parent` forbids it so that a figure cannot arrive by a route that skips every rung and loses which disclosure it came from, and it says where a caption belongs instead — on the PART. The consequence is measurable here: China SCE prints "Due to related parties 應付關聯方款項" 2,588,416 on the face of its balance sheet, and that row now reaches no concept. It used to be swept into `bs_cl__other_current_liabilities` — a related-party payable published as an unexplained remainder — and it is now refused from there by the residual's own "dedicated not tested" prohibition and reported for review naming this line. Recovering it properly needs a FACE part, the shape `sub__rp_find_1` declares for the receivable and which nothing fills yet.

items.label: Customer's Name
items.definition: Legal name of the reporting customer or entity for which the financial statements are presented. Use the legal entity name presented on the financial statements, cover page or corporate information section. Retain legal suffixes and the reported language.

items.definition: Scope of the financial statements, such as consolidated, separate, standalone, company-only or combined. Use the explicit scope stated in the title or basis-of-preparation note.

items.label: Rounding
items.definition: Reported scaling or rounding basis applied to monetary values in the financial statements. Capture the scale exactly as reported, then map it to the controlled value.

items.label: Source Currency
items.definition: Currency in which the source financial statements are presented. Use the presentation currency explicitly stated in the statements or accounting-policy note. Return ISO 4217 code where determinable.

items.label: Target Currency
items.definition: Currency required by the target spreading or downstream system. Extract only when explicitly supplied in the template, instruction or system metadata.

items.label: Statement Date
items.definition: Financial statement reporting date or period end date. For annual or interim statements, use the end date of the reporting period.

items.label: Periods
items.definition: Number of months covered by the current reporting period. Derive from explicit current-period start and end dates or explicit duration when available.

items.label: Total Assets
items.definition: Control total equal to total assets for the current reporting date. Populate from the referenced canonical key in the existing statement ontology.

items.label: Total Equity & Reserves & Liab
items.definition: Control total equal to total equity and liabilities for the current reporting date. Populate from the referenced canonical key in the existing statement ontology.

items.label: Total Income & Expenses
items.definition: Control result from the income statement for the current reporting period. Populate from the referenced canonical key in the existing statement ontology.

items.label: Unexplained Adj to Ret Profits
items.definition: Residual control needed to reconcile opening retained profits, current-period movements and closing retained profits. Populate from the referenced canonical key in the existing statement ontology.

items.label: Difference
items.definition: Balance-sheet reconciliation difference between total assets and total equity and liabilities. Calculate after both control totals have been populated.

items.label: Audit Opinion(Stmt Source)
items.definition: Type of external auditor opinion expressed on the financial statements. Classify from the formal audit opinion paragraph.

items.label: Accounting Standard
items.definition: Financial reporting framework explicitly used to prepare the statements. Use the explicit framework in the basis-of-preparation or auditor report.

items.label: Accountant
items.definition: Name of the external auditor or reporting accountant associated with the financial statements. Use the audit firm signing the report; capture engagement partner separately only if another ontology requires it.

items.label: Analyst
items.definition: Analyst assigned to prepare or review the financial spread. Populate from workflow metadata or user input.

items.label: Statement type
items.definition: Frequency or reporting nature of the source statements. Use explicit document title and reporting period.

items.label: Status
items.definition: Workflow status of the extraction or financial spread. Populate from workflow state.

items.label: Reconcile To
items.definition: Comparative reporting date against which the current-period statement is reconciled. Use the comparative column date corresponding to the current statement.

items.label: Contingent liabilities
items.definition: Contingent liabilities disclosed in the notes — possible obligations that are not recognised on the balance sheet: corporate and bank guarantees given, performance bonds, letters of credit, litigation and claims outstanding, and tax disputes. Disclosed only in the notes, so the amount guaranteed and the amount utilised are stated there and are different figures. Capture the complete relevant disclosure with note number, reporting period, currency, unit, scope and exact source location. Preserve separate amounts and categories as structured child facts where available. Guarantees, letters of credit, performance bonds and bank guarantees, summed by type.
items.decomposition_rule: Classify each unique item in the fixed §5 priority order (Letters of Credit, Performance bonds, Bank guarantees, Corporate guarantees, then unclassified); never split or fabricate an exposure.
items.note_use_rationale: A contingent liability is disclosed only in the notes, so there is no face amount for a note to corroborate; evidence_only would make this concept unfillable by any route.

cascade.note: §6.1 primary. The four classified type totals — Letters_of_Credit_Total + Performance_Bonds_Total + Bank_Guarantees_Total + Corporate_Guarantees_Total — read from the dedicated contingent-liabilities / contingencies note (whose title pattern also matches the combined 承诺及或有事项 / Commitments and contingencies heading; capital and lease commitments are vetoed at row level). All four terms are any_of because a filing discloses whatever subset of the four it has, and the four children partition that note's rows by instrument qualifier in §5 priority order (LC vetoes nothing, PB vetoes LC, BG vetoes LC+PB, corporate vetoes LC+PB+BG), so summing them cannot count one row twice. refuse_negative: this rung computes an exposure, so a negative result means the rows were not what it assumed.

§3's amount selection. The dedicated external-guarantee note (对外担保 / 担保事项 / Guarantees given), at the AMOUNT UTILISED — the outstanding guarantee balance, "the most specific outstanding exposure". This is a RUNG, not a term of CL_P1: §6.4 says the same guarantee is repeated across 或有负债 and 对外担保 and must be treated as one item, so the two notes are alternative sources of a single figure and adding them would double count. refuse_negative: an outstanding exposure cannot be negative.

§3 fallback, and the place where AMOUNT GUARANTEED is kept apart from AMOUNT UTILISED. The same external-guarantee note read at the contracted amount guaranteed, used only when the note prints no outstanding balance — never added to CL_P2's figure, because the two are different amounts for one exposure. Guarantees released or repaid in the period (已解除担保金额 / 本期解除担保金额 / 已偿还金额) are deducted: the contracted amount still contains them and §3 forbids either as the exposure figure. The deduction is role adjustment with sign -1, so it can never make this rung resolve on its own — a released amount alone has nothing to be deducted from. refuse_negative: releases exceeding the contracted amount mean the two rows were not the pair this rung assumed.

§2 and §6.4: filings that carry the guarantees only inside the related-party disclosure (关联方担保 / 关联担保), at the AMOUNT UTILISED. Its own rung for the same repeated-disclosure reason as CL_P2 — 关联方担保 is one of the five notes §6.4 names as re-stating the same exposure, so it may substitute for the notes above but never be summed with them.

The related-party disclosure read at the AMOUNT GUARANTEED, when no outstanding balance is printed there. Sits below CL_P4 exactly as CL_P3 sits below CL_P2: §3 ranks the outstanding exposure first, and the guaranteed and utilised figures may never both be counted.

§6.3 last resort. The note's own reported total (Total guarantees / 担保金额合计 / 总担保金额 / 或有负债合计), ALONE in its rung. A filing that itemises no components is the only case where the total is the answer; because no rung may combine the total with components, and rungs are tried in order with the first that resolves winning, the total is reachable only when every rung above it failed — which is precisely "Use 60 and 40 for type totals. Do not calculate 100 + 60 + 40."

items.definition:
The total depreciation charged for the period on property, plant and equipment, including right-of-use assets where the note presents them together — the charge recognised in profit or loss during the period, whatever functions it was charged to. It is disclosed as the depreciation line of the movement schedule inside the property, plant and equipment note, or in the fixed asset or right-of-use asset note of a filing that heads that asset class differently, in English or in Chinese. It is not the accumulated depreciation carried at either end of the period, nor the cost or net carrying amount of the assets.

Take the period's depreciation charge from the asset note's movement schedule, not the accumulated depreciation balance or carrying amount, and treat it as depreciation for all functions rather than the operating-expense share. Depreciation rows inside the note that PP&E note names.

items.definition:
The amortisation charged for the period on prepaid land lease payments — the amount released to profit or loss over the lease term, which some filings caption as a release rather than an amortisation. It is disclosed inside the note for prepaid lease payments or prepaid land lease payments, under those headings or their Chinese equivalents, or in the right-of-use asset note that superseded them. It is not the unamortised balance of the prepayment at either end of the period, nor the split of that balance into current and non-current portions, and it is not an accumulated amortisation figure or an amount transferred out, disposed of or written off during the period.

Take the amount released or amortised to profit or loss during the period, never the remaining prepaid lease balance or its current and non-current split. Depreciation rows inside the note that Prepaid lease payments note names.

items.definition:
The depreciation or amortisation that the profit-before-tax note states was charged to an operating-expense function — administrative, general and administrative, selling, distribution, marketing, operating, or research and development or other operating expenses. The qualifier in the caption is what makes it this figure: the note commonly discloses several depreciation amounts, and only the one tied to one of those functions belongs here. It is disclosed in the note itemising what profit or loss before taxation is arrived at after charging, or under the Traditional or Simplified Chinese equivalent of that profit-before-tax heading. It is STATED IN A SENTENCE of that note and never taken from one of its tabulated rows. It is not the note's unqualified total depreciation, and it is not the amount the same note qualifies as charged to cost of sales; both read as depreciation in the same place but are different quantities.

Take only the depreciation amount whose caption names an operating-expense function, never the note's unqualified total depreciation nor the amount it qualifies as charged to cost of sales. The operating-expense depreciation callout inside the profit-before-tax note. Identified by the QUALIFIER in the caption (administrative, selling, distribution, operating, R&D, other oprating) rather than by the note alone.

items.definition:
The total depreciation for the period as the profit-before-tax note reports it in a single unqualified row — the charge across every function, before any split between cost of sales and operating expenses. It is disclosed in the note itemising what profit or loss before taxation is arrived at after charging, or under the Traditional or Simplified Chinese equivalent of that profit-before-tax heading. It is not any caption in that note qualified by a function, whether cost of sales or an operating-expense function, since each of those is a share of this figure rather than the figure. Nor is it itself the depreciation charged to operating expenses, which is what remains once the cost-of-sales share is deducted.

Take the note's unqualified total depreciation row, never a caption qualified by cost of sales or by an operating-expense function, and remember the cost-of-sales share still has to be deducted from it. The sum of depreciation rows inside the profit-before-tax note.

items.definition:
The depreciation and amortisation charge borne by cost of sales — the part of the period's depreciation of property, plant and equipment, fixed assets, right-of-use assets, investment property or construction in progress, and of amortisation or release of prepaid lease payments, that has been absorbed into the cost of goods sold or of services rendered. It is STATED IN A SENTENCE of the note that breaks down cost of sales, cost of revenue, cost of services or direct operating costs, or of the profit-before-tax or asset notes — never taken from a tabulated row of any of them, because a row that appears to state this share is almost always the note total the share is a component of. It is not the cost of sales amount itself, nor any other subtotal of that note, and it is not the period's total depreciation charge across all functions, of which this is only the production share. It is also not a movement line lifted from a fixed-asset schedule — opening or closing carrying amounts, accumulated depreciation, disposals, transfers, write-offs or exchange differences — and not an impairment loss.

Beyond the cost of sales note, this values could be available in profit before taxation note prose or asset related notes. It will specifically call out depreciation included in cost of sales, never included depreciation with regards to administrative expenses or other operating expenses.
You might add up values across different notes only if they are for items of same nature like different types of fixed assets, but never profit before taxation and fixed asset note.

items.definition:
The single closing total carrying amount that a note on financial assets measured at fair value through profit or loss reports for the holdings it classifies as current assets, one figure covering every instrument class the note lists at the reporting date. It is disclosed inside the note headed as financial assets at fair value through profit or loss, financial assets at FVTPL or held-for-trading investments or securities, and the Traditional and Simplified Chinese equivalents of those headings. It is not any component row within that note: not a listed or unlisted, quoted or unquoted, equity- or debt-securities class subtotal, not the derivative or other-receivable lines, not a fair-value-level row, and not an opening balance, addition, purchase, disposal, redemption, transfer or exchange-difference movement row. It is also not the balance-sheet face line for securities and other financial assets, and not the total of a different measurement-category note such as the FVTOCI, available-for-sale, held-to-maturity or debt-investments note.

Read only the closing grand total of the FVTPL current-asset note itself, never a class subtotal, component or movement row inside it, and never a total belonging to another measurement-category note. The current-asset FVTPL note (spec 5.1). Reads that note's TOTAL row and nothing else, because spec 5.3 defines Find_1_CP = SUM(unique note_total ...) — so this child deliberately overrides the shared veto on total/合計/合计/總額/总额 and instead vetoes everything a component row could be. This same note is also read by three siblings (included derivatives, included other receivables, non-current split), so it is kept distinguishable by row_caption_any_override matching only total captions and by row_caption_none_override vetoing exactly the qualifiers those siblings own — derivative/衍生, other receivable/其他應收/其他应收, the current and non-current split callouts, level captions — plus class subtotals (listed/unlisted, equity/debt securities, 上市, 股本證券) so a class subtotal is never added to the grand total, and never the note total to its own line items (spec 3.3).

items.definition:
The single closing total carrying amount that a note on financial assets measured at fair value through other comprehensive income reports for the holdings it classifies as current assets, one figure covering every instrument class the note lists at the reporting date. It is disclosed inside the note headed as financial assets at fair value through other comprehensive income or financial assets at FVTOCI, their Traditional and Simplified Chinese equivalents, and the PRC-GAAP heading for equity instrument investments measured that way. It is not the total of the fair-value-through-profit-or-loss note, which the neighbouring heading differs from only on other comprehensive income versus profit or loss, and it is not the available-for-sale or debt-investments total. Nor is it any row inside the FVTOCI note itself: not a listed or unlisted, equity- or debt-securities class subtotal, not a derivative, other-receivable, impairment or fair-value-level line, and not a movement row of the year's reconciliation.

Read only the closing grand total of the FVTOCI current-asset note, never a component or movement row inside it, and never the profit-or-loss note's total in its place. The current-asset FVTOCI note (spec 5.1). Same deliberate total-row read as the FVTPL sibling and for the same reason (Find_1_CP is a sum of note totals, spec 5.3), so it overrides the shared total veto. Its note title cannot collide with the FVTPL child: the two titles differ on 'through profit or loss' versus 'through other comprehensive income' / 損益 versus 其他全面收益, and each was tested to claim only its own heading. 其他权益工具投资 is included as the PRC-GAAP name for FVTOCI equity instruments.

items.definition:
The closing total carrying amount that a note on available-for-sale financial assets, or a note on held-to-maturity financial assets, reports for the holdings it classifies as current assets, taken from each such note's own total row where a filing prints both headings as separate notes. It is disclosed under those pre-IFRS-9 headings, including their forms as available-for-sale or held-to-maturity investments or securities and the Traditional and Simplified Chinese equivalents. Because these headings themselves contain the words sale and maturity, it is not a proceeds-from-sale, disposal, redemption or amount-received-on-maturity row, all of which are movements during the period rather than the balance held at the reporting date. It is also not a listed or unlisted, equity- or debt-securities class subtotal inside the note, not an impairment or loss-allowance line, and not part of FVTPL or FVTOCI.

Take each available-for-sale or held-to-maturity note's own closing total and never a sale, disposal, redemption or maturity movement row that the heading's own wording invites, nor a class subtotal inside the note. The pre-IFRS-9 headings still printed by many filings: available-for-sale financial assets and held-to-maturity financial assets (spec 5.1). One child because a filing that prints both prints them as two separately titled notes and this child reads each note's own total row; it never sums a total with its components (spec 3.3). Note the veto asymmetry that made this child possible: the shared veto list must not contain a bare 'sale', 'maturity', 出售 or 到期, since those substrings live inside these two headings — they are anchored (^出售, 到期贖回) throughout this family for that reason.

items.definition:
The closing total carrying amount that a note headed with one of the securities names that are current by nature reports at the reporting date, namely investment securities, marketable securities, money market instruments or short-term money market deposits and their Traditional and Simplified Chinese equivalents. A filing prints at most one of these as a note heading, and the figure is that note's own total across the securities, funds, bonds, instruments or deposits it lists. It is not an individual security, fund, bond, wealth-management product or deposit row inside the note, and not a listed or unlisted class subtotal. It is also not cash and cash equivalents or bank balances and deposits, which are disclosed in their own note even where a short-term money-market deposit resembles them, and not a total belonging to any of the measurement-category notes.

Take the whole total of the investment, marketable or money-market securities note and never an individual instrument or deposit row inside it, nor any figure from the cash and bank balances note. The four remaining spec 5.1 headings that are current by nature and that spec 6.1 explicitly withholds from LTP: investment securities, marketable securities, money market instruments and short-term money market deposits (投資證券 / 有價證券 / 貨幣市場工具 / 短期貨幣市場存款 and simplified forms). items.definition:
The closing total carrying amount that a residual financial-asset note reports for the holdings it classifies as current assets, disclosed under headings such as other financial assets, a bare financial assets note, or structured deposits including structured deposits with embedded derivatives, together with their Traditional and Simplified Chinese equivalents. The figure is the note's own total across the instruments it lists, so where a structured-deposit note totals its deposits inclusive of their embedded derivative element that inclusive total is the amount. It is not the embedded derivative element disclosed as a separate line, nor a wealth-management product, certificate-of-deposit or individual instrument row inside the note. It is also not the total of a note on other non-current financial assets, whose heading contains this one as a substring but which belongs to the long-term field, and not the total of the FVTPL, FVTOCI or debt-investments notes.

Take the other financial assets or structured deposits note's own current-asset total, never a separately disclosed embedded derivative or instrument row inside it, and never a non-current counterpart of the same heading. The residual spec 5.1 headings: 'Other financial assets', the bare 'Financial asset(s)' note, and structured deposits with embedded derivatives (其他金融資產 / 結構性存款 / 含嵌入式衍生工具的結構性存款). The bare form is anchored ^...$ so it cannot swallow the FVTPL, FVTOCI or AFS notes its five siblings own, and 'other financial assets' is matched only as a contiguous phrase so 'Other non-current financial assets' / 其他非流動金融資產 is left to LTP (spec 6.1). One veto had to be narrowed for this child specifically: the total-row veto matches derivatives only at the start of a caption, otherwise 'Total structured deposits with embedded derivatives' — this note's own total — would be vetoed by its own heading.

items.definition:
The part of a financial-asset note's total that the note itself states is classified as non-current, shown against a caption such as non-current portion, analysed for reporting purposes as non-current, due after one year, or expected to be recovered or settled more than twelve months after the reporting date, and the Traditional and Simplified Chinese equivalents. It is disclosed as a split-out line inside the very notes whose totals are read for this field, that is the notes on financial assets at fair value through profit or loss or through other comprehensive income, available-for-sale or held-to-maturity financial assets, debt investments, investment and money-market securities, and other financial assets or structured deposits. It is not the current portion of that same split, whose caption differs from it by only one word and which is the part that stays in this field, and it is not the note's own total. Nor is it the total of a separate note on non-current or long-term financial assets, since only an amount sitting inside a total already extracted here may be taken out of it.

Take only the non-current portion that the note carves out of its own total, never the current portion beside it and never the note total itself. The 'Analysed for reporting purposes as:' non-current callout inside the very notes the six Find_1 children read (note_title_any repeats their six titles verbatim). Spec 5.1 admits only amounts classified under Current Assets and spec 8 requires the classification to match the target field, so where one note total spans both portions the note's own non-current line is removed from it — the deduction is by construction inside the total that was extracted (spec 3.3). Distinguished from the note-total children by row_caption_any_override matching only non-current qualifiers, and every current/non-current veto in both directions is anchored (^current, ^流動, 列作流動 versus non-current, 非流動, 列作非流動) because 'non-current portion' contains 'current portion' as a substring and an unanchored veto would silently kill this child. Enters both rungs as an optional adjustment: absent a split it finds nothing and nothing is deducted.

items.definition:
The carrying amount of derivative assets that sits inside the total of a current financial-asset note, shown there under captions such as derivative financial instruments, embedded derivatives, forward foreign exchange contracts, interest rate or cross-currency swaps and option contracts, together with their Traditional and Simplified Chinese equivalents. It is disclosed as a line item within the same notes whose totals are read for this field, so the amount is by construction part of a figure already extracted. It is not that note's own total, and not a derivatives subtotal standing above the individual derivative rows beneath it. It is also not a derivative amount reported anywhere else in the filing, whether a standalone derivative financial instruments note, the balance-sheet face line, a derivative liability, or a derivative shown as non-current, because only a derivative demonstrably included in the extracted total may be deducted from it.

Take a derivative row from inside a note whose total was read, never that note's own total, and never a derivative figure disclosed elsewhere in the filing. The first Find_2_CP component, spec 4.2 / 5.2 included_derivatives. note_title_any repeats the six Find_1 note titles verbatim, so a derivative can only be deducted from inside a note whose total was actually extracted — spec 3.3 requires a deduction to be demonstrably included in the extracted note total and forbids deducting a component merely because the term appears elsewhere in the filing. Reads the same notes as the note-total children and is distinguished by row_caption_any_override on derivative captions only (derivative financial instruments, embedded derivatives, forwards, swaps, options, 衍生工具 / 衍生金融工具 / 嵌入式衍生工具 / 遠期外匯合約 / 利率互换). It keeps the shared veto unchanged, total row included, so a 'Total derivatives' subtotal is never added to the derivative rows beneath it; the shared non-current veto also keeps a derivative disclosed as non-current out of this current-portion figure. Optional adjustment, sign -1: spec 5.3 permits Find_2_CP to be zero when the notes were found and no such component sits in their totals.

items.definition:
The amount of other receivables that sits inside the total of a current financial-asset note, shown there under a caption such as other receivables or other receivables, prepayments and deposits, and the Traditional and Simplified Chinese equivalents. It is disclosed as a line item within the same notes whose totals are read for this field, so the amount is by construction part of a figure already extracted. It is not that note's own total, and not a total other receivables subtotal placed above its own components. It is also not the trade receivables figure, not amounts due from related parties, associates or joint ventures, and not the total of a standalone other receivables, prepayments and deposits note or the balance-sheet face line for it, since only an amount proven to sit inside the extracted note total may be deducted from it.

Take an other-receivables row from inside a note whose total was read, never that note's total, the trade receivables figure, or a standalone receivables note or face line. The second and last Find_2_CP component, spec 4.2 / 5.2 included_other_receivables. Same six note titles as its derivative sibling, for the same inclusion-proof reason (spec 3.3), and distinguished from it by row_caption_any_override on other-receivable captions only (other receivables, 其他應收款項 / 其他應收賬款 / 其他应收款), which share no row with the derivative patterns — checked against the same caption set. Deliberately narrow: spec 4.2 closes with 'The CP field deducts only derivatives and other receivables', so trade receivables and amounts due from related parties are not matched, and no child here deducts investments in related parties, associates or joint ventures — spec 4.2 and 6.3 assign those to LTP alone. It keeps the shared veto, total row included, so a 'Total other receivables' subtotal cannot be added to its own components. Optional adjustment, sign -1 (spec 5.3).

items.definition:
The total fair value of financial assets measured using Level 3 inputs, that is significant unobservable inputs, as reported at the reporting date. It is disclosed in the note setting out the fair value hierarchy or fair value measurement of financial instruments, including the Traditional and Simplified Chinese forms of the fair value hierarchy, level and measurement headings. It is not the Level 1 or Level 2 amount, not the hierarchy table's grand total across all three levels, and not the Level 3 total reported in the liabilities half of the same table. Nor is it a row of the Level 3 reconciliation, such as a transfer into or out of Level 3, purchases, issues, settlements or fair-value gains and losses, nor a valuation-technique, unobservable-input or sensitivity narrative row.

Take the Level 3 total for financial assets at fair value only, never Level 1 or Level 2, never the table's all-levels grand total or its liabilities column, and never a Level 3 reconciliation movement row.

items.label: Revenue on Face of the statement
items.definition:
Revenue or turnover or sales earned in the period as printed on the face of the income statement itself — the top line in most cases, stated before cost of sales and other revenue generally. It is read from the consolidated statement of profit or loss, comprehensive income or income statement.

For certain type of entities like Banks / Financial institutions, this maybe named as Interest Income.

items.definition:
Objective is to identify what is the breakup of revenue provided in the note and then classify each of the line item as principal business or not. Principal business is identified basis the industries the entity is operating in, sometime the entity itself might provide other income/other revenue in the breakup which can be kept aside and rest can be consumed. Never consume total revenue or sub totals as a part of this line item.
For example: Interest income should be considered if the entity has banking / FI operations, Rental Income should be considered if there is real estate exposure.

Ensure when you are adding up values you do not add up values across different brakdowns as it could lead to double counting. So thing like breakup by country, segment, etc. may not be factored into summation when there is a table already being used.

items.definition:
The face amount of letters of credit outstanding at the reporting date — documentary credits, standby credits, and irrevocable or unexpired credits opened on the entity's behalf — carried as an exposure that is not recognised on the balance sheet. It is disclosed inside the contingent liabilities or contingencies note, including the combined commitments and contingencies heading (或有负债 / 或有事项 / 承诺及或有事项). It is not the note's own total of contingent liabilities or guarantees, it is not the credit facility limit, credit line or undrawn amount the bank has made available, and it is not a movement row such as credits issued, expired or cancelled during the period.

Take only rows whose caption names a letter of credit or a documentary or standby credit, never the note's own total and never a credit facility limit, credit line or undrawn amount. Letters of credit in the contingent-liabilities / contingencies note (§4.2): 信用证, 已开立/未结/未到期/不可撤销/备用/跟单信用证, documentary and standby credits. Four children read this ONE note and are told apart by the INSTRUMENT QUALIFIER in the caption, never by the note, so no row is claimed twice. This is §5's priority 1, so it vetoes no other instrument and keeps the shared veto list unchanged (the shared 已到期 veto is deliberately not bare 到期, so 未到期信用证 still selects).

items.definition:
The amount of performance bonds and performance guarantees in force at the reporting date — instruments that secure the entity's own performance of a contract or construction obligation (履约保函 / 履约担保 / 履约保证金). It is disclosed inside the contingent liabilities or contingencies note, among the other guarantee instruments listed there. It is not a letter of credit: where a single caption names both instruments, the letter of credit is the more specific reading and owns the row. It is also not a refundable performance deposit paid over and carried as a receivable, which is an asset rather than an exposure, and not the note's own total.

Take only rows whose caption names a performance bond, performance guarantee or 履约保函, never a caption that also names a letter of credit and never a refundable performance deposit held as a receivable. Performance bonds in the same contingency note (§4.3): 履约保函, 履约保证, 履约担保, 合同/工程履约保函. Distinguished from the letter-of-credit child by qualifier and it VETOES the letter-of-credit captions, because §5 ranks Letters of Credit above Performance bonds — a caption naming both belongs to the LC child. It also vetoes 其他应收款 / 可退还保证金 so an ordinary refundable 履约保证金 deposit asset is not counted as an exposure (§4.3's caveat).

items.definition:
The amount of guarantees a bank has issued on the entity's behalf and that remain in force at the reporting date — payment and advance-payment guarantees, bid and tender guarantees, and financing or non-financing guarantees (银行保函 / 银行保证 / 银行出具的保函). It is disclosed inside the contingent liabilities or contingencies note. It is not a letter of credit and not a performance bond: both are more specific instruments, and a caption naming either of them belongs to that line rather than here. It is also not the banking facility or credit limit granted, which measures available capacity rather than exposure.

Take only rows whose caption names a bank guarantee or 银行保函, never a caption that also names a letter of credit or performance bond, and never a facility or credit limit. Bank guarantees in the same contingency note (§4.4): 银行保函, 银行保证, 银行出具的保函, 融资性/非融资性保函, 付款/预付款/投标保函, bid and tender guarantees. Vetoes the letter-of-credit AND performance-bond captions, because §5 puts both above Bank guarantees — the qualifier, not the note, decides ownership.

row_terms: guarantees in respect of banking facilities

items.definition:
The amount of guarantees the entity has itself given over another party's obligations — for subsidiaries, associates, joint ventures, related parties, customers or suppliers — including joint and several suretyship and guarantees over banking facilities, loans or borrowings granted to those parties (对外担保 / 公司担保 / 企业担保 / 连带责任保证). It is disclosed inside the contingent liabilities or contingencies note, where it is the broadest of the guarantee labels. It is not the guaranteed borrowing or facility itself, which is a recognised liability of the party that owes it rather than a contingent exposure of the guarantor. It is also not a bank-issued instrument: a caption that also names a letter of credit, a performance bond or a bank guarantee belongs to that more specific instrument line.

Take only rows describing a guarantee the entity gives over another party's obligation, never the guaranteed borrowing itself and never a caption that also names a letter of credit, performance bond or bank guarantee. Corporate and related-party guarantees in the same contingency note (§4.1): 公司/企业担保, 对外担保, 关联方担保, 为子公司/联营/合营/关联方提供担保, 债务/借款/融资担保, 连带责任保证, 保证责任, and the English "guarantees given in respect of banking facilities granted to subsidiaries" form. It is the broadest label, so it vetoes letters of credit, performance bonds AND bank guarantees — §4.1's explicit sentence plus §5's own two examples (对外担保 + 履约保函 → Performance bonds; 关联方担保 + 银行保函 → Bank guarantees), both verified against these patterns.

items.definition:
The guarantee exposure still outstanding at the reporting date — the portion of the guarantees given that has actually been utilised or drawn down, or the guarantee balance remaining in force at period end (担保余额 / 担保责任余额 / 实际担保金额 / 尚未履行金额 / 未结金额). It is disclosed in the dedicated guarantees-given note (对外担保 / 对外提供担保 / 担保事项 / Guarantees given), where it is printed alongside, and is normally smaller than, the amount guaranteed. It is not that contracted amount guaranteed or guarantee limit, which is a different quantity for the same guarantee and may never be counted with it. It is also not the opening balance of the period and not the note's own aggregate total line.

Take the outstanding or utilised guarantee balance at period end, never the contracted amount guaranteed, never the opening balance and never the note's total. The dedicated external-guarantee note (对外担保 / 担保事项 / Guarantees given) read at the AMOUNT UTILISED: 担保余额, 担保责任余额, 实际担保金额, 尚未履行金额, 未结金额, amount utilised / drawn / outstanding. This is §3's "most specific outstanding exposure". Three children read this note, so each carries its own qualifier: this one owns the outstanding-balance captions and the amount-guaranteed child vetoes them. Its veto list drops ONLY the closing-balance patterns (closing balance / 期末 / 年末) — for a contingent exposure the period-end guarantee balance IS the figure — while the opening-balance veto (期初 / 年初 / opening balance) is kept, so 期末担保余额 selects and 期初担保余额 does not.

items.definition:
The contracted amount guaranteed — the maximum exposure the guarantee contracts create, whether or not any of it has been drawn (担保金额 / 合同担保金额 / 担保限额 / maximum amount of guarantees). It is disclosed in the dedicated guarantees-given note (对外担保 / 对外提供担保 / 担保事项 / Guarantees given), and it is the figure to use only where that note prints no outstanding guarantee balance. It is not the amount utilised or the outstanding guarantee balance, which is a separate and usually smaller figure for the very same guarantee and must never be added to this one. Nor is it the credit facility or credit limit granted to the borrower, the cumulative amount transacted, or a provision already recognised in respect of the guarantee.

Take the contracted or maximum amount guaranteed, and only where the note prints no outstanding balance — never the utilised or outstanding balance, and never a facility limit or recognised provision. The SAME external-guarantee note read at the AMOUNT GUARANTEED: 担保金额, 合同担保金额, 担保限额, amount guaranteed, maximum guarantee / exposure. This is NOT the amount utilised and §3 ranks it below the outstanding exposure, so the two are separate children in separate rungs and are never summed. It therefore VETOES every outstanding-balance caption the balance child owns (担保…余额, 实际担保金额, 尚未履行金额, 未结金额, amount utilised / drawn) — which also stops 实际担保金额 being claimed here through the substring 担保金额. The shared vetoes keep out 授信额度, 合同总额, 累计发生额, 交易金额 and 已确认预计负债, which §3 forbids as the exposure amount, and the 增加/新增 vetoes stop 本期增加担保金额 movement rows.

The amount of guarantees that ceased during the reporting period — guarantees released, discharged, cancelled or terminated, and amounts repaid or returned in the period (已解除担保金额 / 本期解除担保金额 / 已偿还金额 / 已归还金额). It is disclosed as a movement row in the dedicated guarantees-given note (对外担保 / 担保事项 / Guarantees given), and it exists here only to be deducted from the contracted amount guaranteed, which still contains it. It is never a contingent liability in its own right. In particular it is not the outstanding guarantee balance and not the amount guaranteed, and it may not stand in for either.

Take the released, discharged or repaid guarantee row only as a deduction from the contracted amount guaranteed, never as an exposure figure of its own. The same external-guarantee note's 已解除担保金额 / 本期解除担保金额 / 已偿还金额 / 已归还金额 rows (guarantees released, discharged or repaid in the period). §3 forbids either figure as the exposure amount, so this child is never a figure in its own right: it appears only as the sign -1 adjustment on CL_P3, whose base is the contracted amount guaranteed and which still contains the released and repaid portions. Both other guarantee-note children veto these captions, and this child drops the disposal and released/repaid vetoes it would otherwise self-block on (English repaid/released/discharged/cancelled/terminated, 减少/处置/…, 已偿还/已解除担保/解除担保) while keeping every other shared veto.

The guarantee exposure for related parties still outstanding at the reporting date — the utilised or drawn portion, or the balance in force at period end, of guarantees given for a parent, subsidiary, associate, joint venture or other related party (担保余额 / 实际担保金额 / 尚未履行金额). It is disclosed inside the related-party note (关联方担保 / 关联担保 / 关联方交易 / related party guarantees or transactions), which is where some filings carry these guarantees instead of a separate guarantees note. It is not the contracted amount guaranteed printed in that same note, not the value or volume of related-party transactions disclosed there, and not an amount due from or due to a related party. Where a contingent-liabilities or guarantees-given note restates the same guarantee, this figure substitutes for that disclosure rather than adding to it.

Take the outstanding or utilised guarantee balance from the related-party note, never the contracted amount guaranteed, never a related-party transaction amount, and never a balance due to or from a related party. The related-party disclosure (关联方担保 / 关联担保 / 关联方交易 / related party guarantees) read at the AMOUNT UTILISED, using the same outstanding-balance vocabulary as the external-guarantee balance child. §6.4 names 或有负债, 关联方担保 and 对外担保 as places the SAME exposure is repeated and orders it treated as one item, so this note is its own cascade rung and never a term summed alongside them. Drops the closing-balance vetoes for the same reason as child 5 (关联方担保期末余额 must select); keeps the opening-balance veto.

items.definition:
The single aggregate figure the filing itself prints for its contingent exposure — total contingent liabilities, total guarantees, or the guarantee total (担保金额合计 / 担保余额合计 / 担保总额 / 总担保金额 / 或有负债合计). It is disclosed as the total line of the contingent-liabilities, contingencies or guarantees-given note. It is the answer only for a filing that gives this one figure and itemises no instrument types; it may never be counted alongside the classified instrument amounts it already contains. It is also not a total of credit facility limits, contract sums or cumulative transacted amounts, none of which measures exposure.

Take the note's own printed total only where the note itemises no instrument types, and never add it to any type amount it already includes. The note's own reported TOTAL: Total guarantees / Total contingent liabilities / 担保金额合计 / 担保余额合计 / 总担保金额 / 担保总额 / 或有负债合计. This is the ONE child that deliberately reads a total row, so it is the only one that lifts the shared total vetoes (total, 合计, 总计, 小计) and, with them, the closing-balance vetoes (期末担保余额合计 is a total); every other child keeps them. It sits ALONE in the last cascade rung, which is how §6.3 ("Do not add a reported total to the components included in that total") is made unbreakable rather than merely intended. It still keeps the §3 do-not-use vetoes, so 授信额度合计 or 合同总额 cannot be read as a total exposure.

items.definition:
The amount at stake in a contingency that is not a guarantee instrument — the claim amount, amount in dispute or estimated financial effect of pending litigation and arbitration, legal claims, contract and tax disputes, product warranty obligations, onerous contracts, environmental liabilities and bill or note recourse (涉案金额 / 诉讼金额 / 仲裁金额 / 未决诉讼 / 未决仲裁 / 预计财务影响). It is disclosed inside the contingent liabilities or contingencies note, or in a dedicated litigation and arbitration note (诉讼及仲裁事项 / 重大诉讼、仲裁事项). It is captured as evidence and reported on its own: it is not part of the quantified guarantee and letter-of-credit exposure and must not be summed with those instrument amounts. It is also not a provision already recognised for the same matter (已确认预计负债), which is a recognised liability rather than a contingency.

Capture the claim, disputed or estimated-effect amount of a litigation, arbitration, dispute or warranty matter as separate evidence only, never adding it to the guarantee instrument amounts and never taking a provision already recognised for that matter. §4.5's unclassified matters and their claim amounts: 未决诉讼, 未决仲裁, 涉案金额, 诉讼/仲裁金额, 合同纠纷, 索赔事项, 税务争议, 产品质量保证, 亏损合同, 环境责任, 票据追索责任, 其他或有事项, 预计财务影响, plus the English litigation / arbitration / dispute / warranty / onerous-contract / recourse forms. EVIDENCE ONLY, and deliberately a term of NO cascade rung: §11 feeds aggregate_by_type_and_currency only with items whose classification is not "Unclassified contingent liability", and §8.3 gives these their own table, so summing them into the parent's quantifiable figure would break the spec. It shares the contingency note with children 1-4 but its captions are disjoint from all four instrument vocabularies, so it can never claim their rows (probed: 未决诉讼涉案金额 and Product warranty claims select here and nowhere else).

items.definition:
The part of a financial-asset note's own carrying amount that the note itself states is classified as non-current, taken from the row that carries the non-current qualifier: Non-current, Non-current portion, Analysed for reporting purposes as non-current, amounts due after more than one year, 非流動部分, 列作非流動. It is disclosed inside the notes that analyse securities and other financial assets, whatever heading a filing uses for them, including financial assets at fair value through profit or loss, financial assets at fair value through other comprehensive income, available-for-sale or held-to-maturity financial assets, debt investments, other financial assets, investment securities or securities investments, and structured deposits, and their 金融資產 / 金融资产 equivalents. It is not the note's combined total where the note covers both halves of the balance, and it is not the current-portion row printed beside it; where a note analyses itself into current and non-current, only the amount the note assigns to non-current belongs here.

Take the row a financial-asset note labels as non-current, never that note's combined current-plus-non-current total and never the current-portion row sitting next to it. The row a financial-asset note uses to state the part of its own total that is classified as NON-CURRENT: 'Non-current', 'Non-current portion', 'Analysed for reporting purposes as: non-current', 非流動部分, 列作非流動資產. Spec 6.1 - 'Only use amounts classified under Non-current Assets for this field' - names this row rather than the note's combined total wherever a note covers both halves, which is why this child owns the first cascade rung. Its note titles are the whole in-scope dictionary of 6.1, so it reads the same notes as children 2-9; it is distinguished from them by REQUIRING the non-current qualifier in the caption (row_caption_any_override), which nothing in the shared total vocabulary matches, and the shared vetoes drop the matching current-portion row so the current half can never land on this line. One figure per note: this row or the note's combined total, never both (spec 3.3).

items.definition:
The total carrying amount of the note that analyses financial assets measured at fair value through profit or loss, read once from that note's own total or carrying-amount line, in the case where the whole note is classified as non-current and prints no current/non-current split. It is disclosed in the note headed financial assets at fair value through profit or loss or FVTPL, and in Chinese under 按公平值計入損益的金融資產 or 以公允價值計量且其變動計入當期損益的金融資產 and their simplified forms. It is not one of the instrument sub-lines the note itemises beneath that total, such as listed or unlisted equity securities, funds, wealth-management products or debt instruments, and it is not a cost, gross amount, impairment, fair-value-movement or fair-value-hierarchy line. Where the note does state a separate non-current portion, that stated portion is the figure and this combined total is not.

Take the fair-value-through-profit-or-loss note's own total once, never an instrument sub-line beneath it and never this total when the note itself states a separate non-current portion. The note total of the 'Financial assets at fair value through profit or loss' note where that note is wholly non-current and prints a total rather than a current/non-current split - one of the note_total values Find_1_LTP sums (spec 6.1, 6.2). Reads the note TOTAL deliberately (spec 3.3 - 'Extract the note total once' and 'Do not add a note total to its underlying line items'), so the shared counting vocabulary matches only total / carrying-amount captions and never the note's instrument sub-lines. sub__ltp_nc_portion_of_fincl_asset_notes reads this same note: it is distinguished by requiring a non-current qualifier in the caption, which nothing in the shared vocabulary matches, and it resolves on an earlier cascade rung - so a note is read once, by one child, never by both.

items.definition:
The total carrying amount of the note that analyses structured deposits, read once from that note's own total or carrying-amount line, where the deposits are classified as non-current and the note prints no current/non-current split. It is disclosed in a note headed structured deposits or structured deposits with embedded derivatives, and in Chinese under 結構性存款 or 含嵌入式衍生工具的結構性存款 and their simplified forms. Because the heading itself names an embedded derivative, such a note commonly shows the derivative element as a component row inside it: that component is not this figure, it is deducted separately, and this line takes only the note's own total. It is also not the principal placed or matured during the period, and not the bank balances or plain time deposits reported as cash and cash equivalents.

Take the structured-deposits note's own total, never the embedded-derivative component row inside it and never a bank balance or plain time deposit reported as cash. The note total of the 'Structured deposits with embedded derivatives' note (結構性存款 / 结构性存款) where that note is classified non-current and prints a total rather than a current/non-current split - one of the note_total values Find_1_LTP sums (spec 6.1, 6.2).
